From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: Pacifica Health — ML fit, safety probes & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick summary and proposed next steps so we all have the same view:

Summary (30 min demo + discovery)
- Primary goal: automate triage and clinician-facing summarization for inbound patient messages (non-emergent).
- Key constraints:/ PHI handling, deterministic refusal on emergency content, audit trails for summarization edits.
- Volume: ~150k messages/month initially, many short free-text notes and a subset of records with scanned attachments.

Model fit observations (from demo load profile):
- For high throughput with low latency, we recommend testing two model families: a smaller dense LLM (eg. an LLaMA-derived 13B quantized variant) for routing/triage, and a stronger 34B quantized model for clinician summaries where precision matters.
- We propose a hybrid routing approach: 13B for classification + policy gating; 34B for final summary generation when policy passes.

Safety / refusal & policy evaluation plan
- Build a focused prompt-set (attached) with: 1) emergency detection probes, 2) PHI masking checks, 3) hallucination stress tests (contradictory context), 4) inappropriate advice scenarios.
- Expected behavior baseline: explicit refusal template for emergent content, sanitized outputs (redaction hints), and deterministic fallback to human review queue.

Proposed next steps
1) NDA & procurement notes: we can start with a two-week eval under our standard POC terms; we'll attach an MA/POC plan and initial benchmarks. (See attachments.)
2) Redwood will run a 2-week benchmark on a small, anonymized sample you provide (<= 5k messages) against the recommended models and return latency/cost/quality matrix + failure-mode examples.
3) Joint safety review session: schedule a 60-min call with your clinical safety lead and our applied ML safety engineer to triage refusal patterns and thresholds.

Deliverables we’ll send by EOD
- pacifica_poc_ma_plan.pdf (POC timeline, acceptance criteria)
- model_benchmarks_v1.csv (initial synthetic benchmarks)
- prompt_set_phase1.txt (recommended probes for safety/refusal)

Please confirm the anonymized sample scope and whether you can sign the attached MA/POC plan. If OK, I’ll loop in Ben to align pricing/term questions and Marissa to scope onboarding.

Thanks,
Lauren

Lauren — thanks for the thorough write-up. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Sample data: we can produce a 4k-message anonymized export next week; will include a ~200-message set flagged as "safety-critical" (examples of emergency phrasing).
2) PHI masking: we need the model to provide redaction suggestions, not attempt irreversible redaction during evaluation (we need to audit). Can your eval harness produce token-level masking candidates and a confidence score?
3) Emergency refusal: can you share an example refusal template? We want to ensure language is clinically appropriate (e.g., avoid phrases like "I am not a doctor" in patient-facing contexts).

Also, can you confirm whether the hybrid routing approach supports synchronous fallbacks (i.e., if 13B flags ambiguous, we route to 34B within the same request window) — what latency hit should we anticipate?

If the MA/POC plan looks standard, we can sign and return it by Tuesday. I’ll also loop our compliance lead if we move forward.

—Emma

Head of Product, Pacifica Health
emma.li@pacificahealth.com
